title: RankingSnapshot
description: One normalized ranking data row, produced by scripts/import_rankings.py from a Semrush export, a manually-prepared CSV, a JSON snapshot, or a hand-transcribed real report/search-result observation. Stored at data/rankings/<market_id>.csv. This is the internal representation every import source is normalized into. `source` records PROVENANCE (where the fact ultimately came from), independent of the mechanical import path -- a human typing up numbers read off a real Semrush report is 'semrush' data, not a guess, even though it arrives via the manual-CSV code path.

keyword.description: Null/ambiguous is fine (and required) when the underlying query combined multiple phrases -- do not force a single keyword string onto blended evidence

organic_position.description: Exact tracked position. Must stay null for an absence/'not present in captured results' observation -- never approximate it as some number just outside the captured range (e.g. do not write 11, 21, 50 for 'not seen in top 10/20/50')

competitor_names.description: Comma-separated names visible in the same SERP -- only names actually confirmed present in THIS capture, not names carried over from unrelated prior research

source.description: semrush_csv/json_snapshot/manual_csv describe the mechanical import path; semrush/google_local_capture (set via import_rankings.py --source-override) record the true external provenance of hand-transcribed real data

observed_at.description: When the underlying report/search was actually generated/captured -- not necessarily when it was imported into this file

exact_rank_verified.description: true only if organic_position/maps_position is a real, exact tracked rank. false for an absence observation ('not present in the captured result set') or any case where the query/capture was ambiguous enough that no specific integer position is defensible -- rescore_leads.py and the scorer must never treat a false here as license to guess a number.

notes.description: Free-text context that doesn't fit a structured field -- e.g. an aggregate keyword-footprint summary, or why exact_rank_verified is false
